name: Marvel
hook: The comic company that went from bankruptcy to the biggest movie franchise on earth.

facts.label: Stan Lee
facts.statement: Stan Lee became editor-in-chief of Timely, later Marvel, in 1942 at age 18 and stayed in the job until 1972.

facts.label: The Avengers
facts.statement: The Avengers debuted in 1963 with Thor and Iron Man; issue one cost 12 cents and a mint copy can fetch $15,000.

facts.label: Toy Biz and Disney
facts.statement: Marvel emerged from bankruptcy in 1998 as part of Toy Biz, then sold to Disney in a deal that made Isaac Perlmutter $400 million.

facts.label: Black Panther
facts.statement: Black Panther's Afro-futuristic costumes won Ruth E. Carter the first Costume Design Oscar for a Black woman; Disney pledged $1 million of the film's proceeds to STEM programs.

facts.label: the X-Men
facts.statement: The X-Men are Marvel's mutant team; Kitty Pryde fights alongside them and names her dragon Lockheed.

facts.label: Blade
facts.statement: Blade, "part man, part vampire, all hero," began a Marvel trilogy in 1998 that ended with Trinity in 2004.
